    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T]
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T) (alpha c d : ℝ)
    (halpha_nonneg : 0 ≤ alpha) (hc_nonneg : 0 ≤ c) (hd_nonneg : 0 ≤ d)
    (hfirst_le_one : decayingBernoulliSuccess c d alpha 0 ≤ 1)
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal) :
    (0 < alpha → ∀ hc_pos : 0 < c,
      ∀ seq :
        OptimalAllocationSequence
          (fun _ => decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
            (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha),
        (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
          (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
            (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).objective a =
              EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
                (fun t =>
                  EconCSLib.pmfExp
                    (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d alpha (a.count t) hc_pos.le
                      hd_nonneg halpha_nonneg hfirst_le_one)
                    rankBernoulliFiniteAllConsumedSampleValue)) ∧
          ∀ t : ItemType T,
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
              Filter.atTop
              (nhds
                (((preferenceLaw t).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha) /
                  ∑ i : ItemType T, ((preferenceLaw i).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha)))) ∧
      (alpha = 0 →
        ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ best : ItemType T,
          (∀ t : ItemType T,
            (preferenceLaw t).toReal ≤ (preferenceLaw best).toReal) →
          (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
            (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).objective a =
                EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
                  (fun t =>
                    EconCSLib.pmfExp
                      (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d alpha (a.count t) hc_nonneg
                        hd_nonneg halpha_nonneg hfirst_le_one)
                      rankBernoulliFiniteAllConsumedSampleValue)) ∧
            (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).IsOptimalAtTotal
                N (allOnTypeAllocation N best)) := by
  constructor
  · intro halpha_pos hc_pos seq
    exact theorem2_iv_positive_alpha_corrected_pmf_source_model_endpoint
      preferenceLaw alpha c d halpha_pos hc_pos hd_nonneg hfirst_le_one
      hpreference_pos seq
  · intro halpha_zero N best hbest
    subst alpha
    exact theorem2_iv_alpha_zero_pmf_source_model_endpoint
      preferenceLaw c d hc_nonneg hd_nonneg (by simpa using hfirst_le_one) N best hbest

    "effective_lean_source_declaration": "theorem proposition2_corrected_finite_and_sequence_source\n    {T : \u2115} [NeZero T]\n    (likelihood : ItemType T \u2192 \u211d) (kseq : \u2115 \u2192 \u2115)\n    (hlike_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < likelihood t)\n    (hkpos : \u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192 0 < kseq N)\n    (hbound :\n      \u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192\n        (kseq N : \u211d) + 1 \u2264\n          (N : \u211d) * uniformSqrtMinShare likelihood - T)\n    (seq :\n      OptimalAllocationSequence\n        (fun N => uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N))) :\n    (\u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192 \u2200 a : CountAllocation T,\n      (uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N)).IsOptimalAtTotal N a \u2192\n        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood).Approx a\n          ((2 * (Fintype.card (ItemType T) : \u211d) + 1) / (N : \u211d))) \u2227\n      seq.toAllocationSequence.ConvergesToProfile\n        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood) := by\n  constructor\n  \u00b7 intro N hNpos a hopt\n    exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_finite_of_paper_bound\n      likelihood N (kseq N) hNpos (hkpos N hNpos) hlike_pos a\n      (hbound N hNpos) hopt\n  \u00b7 exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_sequence_homogeneity_of_paper_bound\n      likelihood kseq hlike_pos hkpos hbound seq",

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem theorem2_ii_corrected_pmf_source_model_endpoint\n    {T : \u2115} [NeZero T]\n    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T) (c d : \u211d)\n    (hc_pos : 0 < c) (hd_nonneg : 0 \u2264 d)\n    (hfirst_lt_one : decayingBernoulliSuccess c d 1 0 < 1)\n    (hpreference_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal)\n    (seq : OptimalAllocationSequence\n      (fun _ => decayingBernoulliTopOneConsumptionModel\n        (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d 1)) :\n    (\u2200 a : CountAllocation T,\n      (decayingBernoulliTopOneConsumptionModel\n        (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d 1).objective a =\n        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw\n          (fun t =>\n            EconCSLib.pmfExp\n              (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d 1 (a.count t) hc_pos.le hd_nonneg\n                (by norm_num) hfirst_lt_one.le)\n              rankBernoulliFiniteTopOneSampleValue)) \u2227\n      \u2200 t : ItemType T,\n        Filter.Tendsto\n          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)\n          Filter.atTop\n          (nhds\n            (((preferenceLaw t).toReal) ^ (1 / (1 + c)) /\n              \u2211 i : ItemType T, ((preferenceLaw i).toReal) ^ (1 / (1 + c)))) := by\n  constructor\n  \u00b7 intro a\n    exact decayingBernoulliTopOneModel_objective_eq_source_experiment\n      preferenceLaw c d 1 a hc_pos.le hd_nonneg (by norm_num) hfirst_lt_one.le\n  \u00b7 exact theorem2_ii_decaying_bernoulli_top_one_formula\n      (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d hc_pos hd_nonneg hfirst_lt_one\n      hpreference_pos seq",

    "effective_lean_source_declaration": "theorem theorem3_log_share_conclusion\n    {T : \u2115} [NeZero T] (B : BernoulliSatisfactionModel T)\n    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)\n    (hpreference : \u2200 t, B.likelihood t = (preferenceLaw t).toReal)\n    (hprob_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < B.successProb t)\n    (hprob_lt_one : \u2200 t, B.successProb t < 1)\n    (hpreference_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal)\n    (seq : OptimalAllocationSequence (fun _ => B.toConsumptionModel)) :\n    \u2200 t : ItemType T,\n      Filter.Tendsto\n        (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)\n        Filter.atTop\n        (nhds\n          (theorem3LogShareWeight B t /\n            \u2211 i : ItemType T, theorem3LogShareWeight B i)) := by\n  have hlike_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < B.likelihood t := by\n    intro t\n    rw [hpreference t]\n    exact hpreference_pos t\n  exact theorem3_varying_success_probability_log_share_formula\n    B hprob_pos hprob_lt_one hlike_pos seq",

Consider the setting in which Xi ∼ D, i.e., conditional item values are drawn from a shared distribution.
This implies that the values of items behave similarly across types and within types, and the platform cannot
easily distinguish between the items in a type. From the perspective of a hiring platform, there may be many
candidates with similar backgrounds (e.g., education or work history), none of whom can be distinguished
from another by the platform. Conditional on a recruiter preferring this background, candidate values can
be modeled as coming from a shared distribution.
We show that for a fixed k, as n grows large, the diversity of Sn,k theoretically varies between equal
representation, proportional representation, and near-complete homogeneity depending on the tail-behavior
of D. In particular, distributions that are bounded or have exponential tails induce at least proportional
representation. Meanwhile, Sn,n is completely homogeneous.

    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T] {Omega : Type*} [Fintype Omega] [DecidableEq Omega]
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)
    (itemLaw : PMF Omega) (value : Omega → ℝ) {xTop xSecond : ℝ}
    (k : ℕ)
    (seq :
      OptimalAllocationSequence
        (fun _ =>
          (TopKValueOracle.common T
            (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k))
    (hk_pos : 0 < k)
    (hxTop_pos : 0 < xTop)
    (hxSecond_nonneg : 0 ≤ xSecond)
    (hsecond_le_top : xSecond ≤ xTop)
    (hsecond_lt_top : xSecond < xTop)
    (hvalue_nonneg : ∀ omega, 0 ≤ value omega)
    (hvalue_le : ∀ omega, value omega ≤ xTop)
    (hvalue_split : ∀ omega, value omega = xTop ∨ value omega ≤ xSecond)
    (htop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => value omega = xTop))
    (hnontop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => ¬ value omega = xTop))

        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
          (fun t =>
            EconCSLib.pmfExp
              (EconCSLib.pmfProduct (Fin (a.count t)) Omega itemLaw)
              (fun sample : Fin (a.count t) → Omega =>
                EconCSLib.Probability.sampleTopKSum
                  (fun i => value (sample i)) k))) ∧
      ∀ t : ItemType T,
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
          Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (T : ℝ))) := by
  exact theorem1_i_finiteDiscrete_iid_exact_source_formula
    preferenceLaw itemLaw value k seq hk_pos hxTop_pos hxSecond_nonneg
    hsecond_le_top hsecond_lt_top hvalue_nonneg hvalue_le hvalue_split
    htop_mass_pos hnontop_mass_pos hpreference_pos

theorem theorem2_iv_corrected_pmf_source_model_endpoint
    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T]
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T) (alpha c d : ℝ)
    (halpha_nonneg : 0 ≤ alpha) (hc_nonneg : 0 ≤ c) (hd_nonneg : 0 ≤ d)
    (hfirst_le_one : decayingBernoulliSuccess c d alpha 0 ≤ 1)
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal) :
    (0 < alpha → ∀ hc_pos : 0 < c,
      ∀ seq :
        OptimalAllocationSequence
          (fun _ => decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
            (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha),
        (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
          (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
            (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).objective a =
              EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
                (fun t =>
                  EconCSLib.pmfExp
                    (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d alpha (a.count t) hc_pos.le
                      hd_nonneg halpha_nonneg hfirst_le_one)
                    rankBernoulliFiniteAllConsumedSampleValue)) ∧
          ∀ t : ItemType T,
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
              Filter.atTop
              (nhds
                (((preferenceLaw t).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha) /
                  ∑ i : ItemType T, ((preferenceLaw i).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha)))) ∧
      (alpha = 0 →
        ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ best : ItemType T,
          (∀ t : ItemType T,
            (preferenceLaw t).toReal ≤ (preferenceLaw best).toReal) →
          (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
            (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).objective a =
                EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
                  (fun t =>
                    EconCSLib.pmfExp
                      (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d alpha (a.count t) hc_nonneg
                        hd_nonneg halpha_nonneg hfirst_le_one)
                      rankBernoulliFiniteAllConsumedSampleValue)) ∧
            (decayingBernoulliAllConsumedConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).IsOptimalAtTotal
                N (allOnTypeAllocation N best)) := by
  constructor
  · intro halpha_pos hc_pos seq
    exact theorem2_iv_positive_alpha_corrected_pmf_source_model_endpoint
      preferenceLaw alpha c d halpha_pos hc_pos hd_nonneg hfirst_le_one
      hpreference_pos seq
  · intro halpha_zero N best hbest
    subst alpha
    exact theorem2_iv_alpha_zero_pmf_source_model_endpoint
      preferenceLaw c d hc_nonneg hd_nonneg (by simpa using hfirst_le_one) N best hbest

Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

semantic_model_items.required_check: Judge the listed dimensions from the expanded Lean surface and the pinned source text, including transparent type aliases, record parameter domains, result-only model records, and the bounded terminal definition dependency surface. Treat any listed local opaque/constant/axiom type head as requiring a checked carrier/refinement bridge before it is ordinary model data. Treat every opaque, ambiguous, tactic-body, or bounded terminal term path as requiring a checked semantic bridge before it is treated as an ordinary numeric or propositional result. Do not infer a source model from any local Lean name. For every dimension, record a source locator, a concrete semantic comparison, and Lean evidence; a detected support, joint-law/state-evolution, conditioning/calibration, expectation-definedness, null-cell/partition, or extended-rate shape also needs a checked bridge declaration or constructor route. For every detected probability-law surface, explicitly compare the source and Lean parameterizations rather than merely saying their parameters are positively related: state both scale/rate/variance conventions, the translation formula, and a checked law or outcome bridge. When the generated joint-law dimension requests source-carrier coherence analysis, identify the source and Lean random-variable carriers, explain why stagewise clocks are one joint source draw (or a source-defined kernel composition) rather than resampling, classify the measure transport, and record any all-rate family bridge.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded binder/result type surface
dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

defects.acceptance_condition: Direct iid Pareto paper-facing endpoints derive the power asymptotic and eventual strict forward-marginal antitonicity from the normalized source law, rather than accepting a cited order-statistic sequence or a concavity certificate.
defects.repair_obligation: Use the normalized Pareto density alpha*x^(-alpha-1) on its support, retain alpha > 1, and state the fixed-rank asymptotic and strict marginal property on valid eventual ranks.
defects.resolution_evidence: AppendixD4Source.lean proves the actual iid Pareto fixed-rank asymptotic and eventual strict marginal result; PaperInterface.lean exposes both corrected source endpoints.
defects.source_claim: Lemma D.4 calls x^(-alpha-1) a Pareto PDF for alpha > 1, omitting its alpha normalizer, and asserts strict concavity over a totalized fixed-rank order-statistic expression without a valid-rank/eventual domain.

defects.status_impact_rationale: The displayed density is not normalized as written. The direct iid route uses the normalized Pareto law and proves the advertised fixed-rank power asymptotic together with the valid eventual strict diminishing-marginal conclusion, so the substantive Theorem 1(iv) route is checked under the corrected model.

defects.acceptance_condition: A paper-facing endpoint visibly assumes integrability and nonnegative common mean, identifies every allocation's all-consumed objective with the preferred-type PMF followed by the finite iid-sample expectation, and proves that an all-on allocation at a likelihood-maximizing type is optimal at every total. It must not assert that the archival conclusion holds for negative means or that all tied optima are concentrated.
defects.repair_obligation: Model the initial preferred-type draw as a finite PMF and, conditional on that draw, the all-consumed slate as a finite iid sample from the common integrable law. Prove the source objective is the resulting two-stage expectation, then require nonnegative common mean before comparing likelihood masses.
defects.resolution_evidence: AllConsumedIidSource.lean constructs the finite iid product law and proves its expected slate value is the common-mean linear objective. PaperInterface.theorem1_v_source_experiment_formula exposes the PMF outer expectation, and PaperInterface.theorem1_v_selected_maximizer_conclusion proves the nonnegative-mean all-on optimum. The selected-optimizer convention is recorded separately in the existing approval addendum rather than being treated as a second defect.
defects.source_claim: Theorem 1 assumes only that the common iid conditional-value law has finite mean, then says that the all-consumed optimum uses a type maximizing p_t. A negative common mean reverses that direction: the all-consumed expected value of an item of type t is p_t times the common mean.
defects.source_locator: WebConf 2024, Theorem 1 header and part (v); PRPKG24AccuracyDiversity.txt:345-347 and 437-438
defects.status_impact_rationale: Finite mean alone does not support the printed likelihood-argmax direction. The corrected result makes the nonnegative-mean condition visible and establishes one selected all-on likelihood maximizer under the literal two-stage source experiment; it does not claim the archival finite-mean-only statement.

defects.acceptance_condition: A paper-facing endpoint exposes q_t>0 and q_t<1 for every type, the actual preferred-type PMF and finite iid Bernoulli experiment, and the logarithmic-share limit. It must not replace the endpoint restriction by an unproved convention or use an unbounded/undefined endpoint expression as a real share weight.
affected_source_locators: WebConf 2024, Theorem 3 header and Equation (9); PRPKG24AccuracyDiversity.txt:605-617
defects.repair_obligation: Restrict the top-one logarithmic-share theorem to typewise Bernoulli parameters in the open interval (0,1), construct the finite iid Boolean law for each selected type and count, and prove the PMF outer objective is its two-stage expectation before applying the optimizer-share theorem.
defects.resolution_evidence: BernoulliIidSource.lean proves the finite iid Bernoulli expectation and the PMF-selected two-stage objective identity. PaperInterface.theorem3_top_one_source_experiment_formula exposes that identity, and PaperInterface.theorem3_log_share_conclusion visibly supplies the strict endpoint conditions and proves the share limit. The all-positive preferred-type support condition remains an explicit model convention rather than a separate source-statement defect.
defects.source_claim: Theorem 3 prints the all-type share weight 1 / log(1 / (1-q_t)) for Bernoulli(q_t) conditional values without excluding q_t=0 or q_t=1. At q_t=0 the denominator is zero, and at q_t=1 the displayed real-valued expression is not a finite defined share weight.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The open Bernoulli domain is necessary for the displayed logarithmic weight to be a finite real-valued all-type share formula. The checked endpoint states 0<q_t<1 for each type and retains the intended top-one conclusion under the literal selected-type and iid-Bernoulli experiment. It does not treat the endpoint cases as archival coverage.

defects.acceptance_condition: A paper-facing endpoint makes the strict upper success-probability bound and the source two-stage finite iid experiment explicit, then proves the uniform asymptotic conclusion. It must not claim universal uniformity at q=1 or hide the boundary by selecting one convenient optimizer.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace q>0 by 0<q<1 for the universal top-one homogeneity result, construct the finite iid Bernoulli source law, and establish the selected-type PMF outer expectation before deriving uniformity from the common success probability.
defects.resolution_evidence: BernoulliIidSource.lean constructs the finite iid Boolean law and proves the selected-type PMF objective identity. PaperInterface.theorem3_top_one_source_experiment_formula exposes that identity, and PaperInterface.corollary3_iid_bernoulli_conclusion exposes the common q in (0,1) conditions and proves uniform homogeneity; its positive preferred-type support is a separately visible model convention, not a second defect.
defects.source_claim: Corollary 3 assumes q>0 and concludes that every top-one optimal sequence is asymptotically uniform. The stated domain includes q=1. With at least two positively likely types and q=1, every allocation that gives each such type at least one item already has top-one success probability one, so nonuniform optimal sequences exist.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The q=1 boundary makes the universal arbitrary-optimizer conclusion false, not merely undefined. The corrected target uses one common q in (0,1) and proves the uniform limit under the literal selected-type PMF and finite iid Bernoulli source experiment, without attributing that restriction to the archival q>0 statement.

model_conventions.checked_scope: AppendixD2DensitySource.lean derives a.e. density zero above M from the literal PDF law, the reflected tail-mass integral identity by interval substitution, local integrability, the CDF-power sandwich, and then the D.2, Lemma 1, and Theorem 1(ii) endpoints. No tail, split, or optimizer certificate is accepted from callers. It does not claim a translated/lower-tail extension outside the recorded nonnegative convention.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The phrase 'D has pdf f_D' is represented by a probability measure equal to Lebesgue volume with density ofReal(f_D), with f_D nonnegative, measurable, and integrable. The Theorem 1(ii) allocation endpoint additionally adopts an a.e. nonnegative conditional-value convention. Given that convention, its lower endpoint L, positive width, and positive M are support normalizations rather than separate claims about every merely upper-bounded translated law.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source proof silently changes from a reflected density to an integral representation of upper-tail mass and then to CDF-power bounds. These are not theorem-name consequences of a function called pdf: they require an actual density measure and enough boundedness/integrability for the expected top-k loss to be well defined. The source says only bounded above, so the nonnegative value-domain convention must remain visible rather than being inferred from the tail formula.

model_conventions.checked_scope: PaperInterface.theorem1_ii_formula, theorem1_iii_formula, theorem1_iv_formula, and corollary1 visibly retain strict positivity of each preferred-type mass. Their PMF-selected source objectives and fixed-k conclusions are checked only on that regular all-coordinate domain. The convention does not provide archival source credit and does not assert a zero-support extension.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the checked fixed-k gamma-share endpoints that assert a limiting representation for every named type, the source-selected preferred-type PMF has strictly positive mass at every type. This is an additional regularity condition on the all-coordinate route, not a claim that the archival model text excluded zero-probability types.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source says only that one type is selected with probabilities p_t, which permits zero masses. The direct all-coordinate optimizer-share arguments use positive weights and finite normalized powers for every coordinate; a zero-probability type instead requires a separate supportwise formulation and optimizer-selection analysis. Recording the restriction prevents that zero-support boundary from being smuggled into a source theorem match.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem2RankBernoulliSource.lean uses EconCSLib.pmfPi, proves the atom formula and both expectations, and the corrected PaperInterface endpoints include those equalities in their conclusions. Top-one adds c>0 and q_1<1 for arbitrary-optimum homogeneity; positive-alpha all-consumed needs q_1<=1; alpha zero uses the recorded selected-optimizer convention.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For each type and finite count, the rank coordinates are independent Boolean variables with rank-specific success parameter c*((i+1)+d)^(-alpha). They are not asserted iid across ranks; cross-type independence is neither asserted nor needed because one preferred type is evaluated.
model_conventions.why_needed: The product top-one objective requires within-type independence, while the all-consumed sum objective only needs the rankwise means. The source uses inconsistent iid wording, so the actual finite PMF and its expectation identities must be checked before asymptotic objective theorems receive source-model credit.

model_conventions.checked_scope: AllConsumedIidSource.lean derives the common-mean linear objective from a finite iid sample law. PaperInterface.theorem1_v_source_experiment_formula and PaperInterface.theorem1_v_selected_maximizer_conclusion separately expose the PMF experiment, integrability, nonnegative mean, and selected all-on likelihood-maximizing optimum. Strict uniqueness remains a separate strengthening, not a claim about every tied optimum.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the all-consumed common-distribution endpoint, the common conditional mean is nonnegative for the weak argmax direction and positive for the unique argmax direction.
model_conventions.why_needed: When every item is consumed, the objective is linear in the common mean. A negative common mean reverses the stated argmax direction, and a zero mean eliminates uniqueness.

theorem theorem1_i_formula
    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T] {Omega : Type*} [Fintype Omega] [DecidableEq Omega]
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)
    (itemLaw : PMF Omega) (value : Omega → ℝ) {xTop xSecond : ℝ}
    (k : ℕ)
    (seq :
      OptimalAllocationSequence
        (fun _ =>
          (TopKValueOracle.common T
            (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k))
    (hk_pos : 0 < k)
    (hxTop_pos : 0 < xTop)
    (hxSecond_nonneg : 0 ≤ xSecond)
    (hsecond_le_top : xSecond ≤ xTop)
    (hsecond_lt_top : xSecond < xTop)
    (hvalue_nonneg : ∀ omega, 0 ≤ value omega)
    (hvalue_le : ∀ omega, value omega ≤ xTop)
    (hvalue_split : ∀ omega, value omega = xTop ∨ value omega ≤ xSecond)
    (htop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => value omega = xTop))
    (hnontop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => ¬ value omega = xTop))
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t : ItemType T, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal) :
    (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
      ((TopKValueOracle.common T
        (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
          (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k).objective a =
        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
          (fun t =>
            EconCSLib.pmfExp
              (EconCSLib.pmfProduct (Fin (a.count t)) Omega itemLaw)
              (fun sample : Fin (a.count t) → Omega =>
                EconCSLib.Probability.sampleTopKSum
                  (fun i => value (sample i)) k))) ∧
      ∀ t : ItemType T,
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
          Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (T : ℝ))) := by
  exact theorem1_i_finiteDiscrete_iid_exact_source_formula
    preferenceLaw itemLaw value k seq hk_pos hxTop_pos hxSecond_nonneg
    hsecond_le_top hsecond_lt_top hvalue_nonneg hvalue_le hvalue_split
    htop_mass_pos hnontop_mass_pos hpreference_pos

    "effective_lean_source_declaration": "theorem proposition2_corrected_finite_and_sequence_source\n    {T : \u2115} [NeZero T]\n    (likelihood : ItemType T \u2192 \u211d) (kseq : \u2115 \u2192 \u2115)\n    (hlike_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < likelihood t)\n    (hkpos : \u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192 0 < kseq N)\n    (hbound :\n      \u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192\n        (kseq N : \u211d) + 1 \u2264\n          (N : \u211d) * uniformSqrtMinShare likelihood - T)\n    (seq :\n      OptimalAllocationSequence\n        (fun N => uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N))) :\n    (\u2200 N, 0 < N \u2192 \u2200 a : CountAllocation T,\n      (uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N)).IsOptimalAtTotal N a \u2192\n        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood).Approx a\n          ((2 * (Fintype.card (ItemType T) : \u211d) + 1) / (N : \u211d))) \u2227\n      seq.toAllocationSequence.ConvergesToProfile\n        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood) := by\n  constructor\n  \u00b7 intro N hNpos a hopt\n    exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_finite_of_paper_bound\n      likelihood N (kseq N) hNpos (hkpos N hNpos) hlike_pos a\n      (hbound N hNpos) hopt\n  \u00b7 exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_sequence_homogeneity_of_paper_bound\n      likelihood kseq hlike_pos hkpos hbound seq",

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem theorem2_iii_corrected_pmf_source_model_endpoint\n    {T : \u2115} [NeZero T]\n    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T) (alpha c d : \u211d)\n    (halpha_gt_one : 1 < alpha) (hc_pos : 0 < c) (hd_nonneg : 0 \u2264 d)\n    (hfirst_lt_one : decayingBernoulliSuccess c d alpha 0 < 1)\n    (hpreference_pos : \u2200 t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal)\n    (seq : OptimalAllocationSequence\n      (fun _ => decayingBernoulliTopOneConsumptionModel\n        (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha)) :\n    (\u2200 a : CountAllocation T,\n      (decayingBernoulliTopOneConsumptionModel\n        (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) c d alpha).objective a =\n        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw\n          (fun t =>\n            EconCSLib.pmfExp\n              (decayingBernoulliFiniteLaw c d alpha (a.count t) hc_pos.le\n                hd_nonneg (le_of_lt (lt_trans zero_lt_one halpha_gt_one))\n                hfirst_lt_one.le)\n              rankBernoulliFiniteTopOneSampleValue)) \u2227\n      \u2200 t : ItemType T,\n        Filter.Tendsto\n          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)\n          Filter.atTop\n          (nhds\n            (((preferenceLaw t).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha) /\n              \u2211 i : ItemType T, ((preferenceLaw i).toReal) ^ (1 / alpha))) := by\n  have halpha_nonneg : 0 \u2264 alpha :=\n    le_of_lt (lt_trans zero_lt_one halpha_gt_one)\n  constructor\n  \u00b7 intro a\n    exact decayingBernoulliTopOneModel_objective_eq_source_experiment\n      preferenceLaw c d alpha a hc_pos.le hd_nonneg halpha_nonneg hfirst_lt_one.le\n  \u00b7 exact theorem2_iii_decaying_bernoulli_top_one_formula\n      (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) alpha c d halpha_gt_one hc_pos hd_nonneg\n      hfirst_lt_one hpreference_pos seq",

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
Consider the setting in which Xi ∼ D, i.e., conditional item values are drawn from a shared distribution.
This implies that the values of items behave similarly across types and within types, and the platform cannot
easily distinguish between the items in a type. From the perspective of a hiring platform, there may be many
candidates with similar backgrounds (e.g., education or work history), none of whom can be distinguished
from another by the platform. Conditional on a recruiter preferring this background, candidate values can
be modeled as coming from a shared distribution.
We show that for a fixed k, as n grows large, the diversity of Sn,k theoretically varies between equal
representation, proportional representation, and near-complete homogeneity depending on the tail-behavior
of D. In particular, distributions that are bounded or have exponential tails induce at least proportional
representation. Meanwhile, Sn,n is completely homogeneous.

be modeled as coming from a shared distribution.

representation. Meanwhile, Sn,n is completely homogeneous.

Treat every opaque, ambiguous, tactic-body, or bounded terminal term path as requiring a checked semantic bridge before it is treated as an ordinary numeric or propositional result. Do not infer a source model from any local Lean name. For every dimension, record a source locator, a concrete semantic comparison, and Lean evidence; a detected support, joint-law/state-evolution, conditioning/calibration, expectation-definedness, null-cell/partition, or extended-rate shape also needs a checked bridge declaration or constructor route. For every detected probability-law surface, explicitly compare the source and Lean parameterizations rather than merely saying their parameters are positively related: state both scale/rate/variance conventions, the translation formula, and a checked law or outcome bridge. When the generated joint-law dimension requests source-carrier coherence analysis, identify the source and Lean random-variable carriers, explain why stagewise clocks are one joint source draw (or a source-defined kernel composition) rather than resampling, classify the measure transport, and record any all-rate family bridge. This individual row has an explicit source-presentation-selected direct map route. The association binds its byte-verified source item and current elaborated signature; it does not assert a direct/Spec structural equivalence.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded binder/result type surface
dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

expanded_shape_basis: generic, finite, subtype, or opaque carrier surface
expanded finite carrier requiring boundary-case review
dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded probability-law type with finite or ordered carrier
transparent terminal definition closure with finite or ordered probability construct
dimensions.required_check: For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded probability-law type surface
transparent terminal definition closure with probability or integration construct
dimensions.required_check: Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

expanded_shape_basis: transparent terminal definition closure with integration or expectation construct
dimensions.required_check: For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

theorem theorem1_i_formula
    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T] {Omega : Type*} [Fintype Omega] [DecidableEq Omega]
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)
    (itemLaw : PMF Omega) (value : Omega → ℝ) {xTop xSecond : ℝ}
    (k : ℕ)
    (seq :
      OptimalAllocationSequence
        (fun _ =>
          (TopKValueOracle.common T
            (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k))
    (hk_pos : 0 < k)
    (hxTop_pos : 0 < xTop)
    (hxSecond_nonneg : 0 ≤ xSecond)
    (hsecond_le_top : xSecond ≤ xTop)
    (hsecond_lt_top : xSecond < xTop)
    (hvalue_nonneg : ∀ omega, 0 ≤ value omega)
    (hvalue_le : ∀ omega, value omega ≤ xTop)
    (hvalue_split : ∀ omega, value omega = xTop ∨ value omega ≤ xSecond)
    (htop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => value omega = xTop))
    (hnontop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => ¬ value omega = xTop))
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t : ItemType T, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal) :
    (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
      ((TopKValueOracle.common T
        (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
          (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k).objective a =
        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
          (fun t =>
            EconCSLib.pmfExp
              (EconCSLib.pmfProduct (Fin (a.count t)) Omega itemLaw)
              (fun sample : Fin (a.count t) → Omega =>
                EconCSLib.Probability.sampleTopKSum
                  (fun i => value (sample i)) k))) ∧
      ∀ t : ItemType T,
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
          Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (T : ℝ))) := by
  exact theorem1_i_finiteDiscrete_iid_exact_source_formula
    preferenceLaw itemLaw value k seq hk_pos hxTop_pos hxSecond_nonneg
    hsecond_le_top hsecond_lt_top hvalue_nonneg hvalue_le hvalue_split
    htop_mass_pos hnontop_mass_pos hpreference_pos

    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T] (B : BernoulliSatisfactionModel T)
    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)
    (hpreference : ∀ t, B.likelihood t = (preferenceLaw t).toReal)
    (hprob_pos : ∀ t, 0 < B.successProb t)
    (hprob_lt_one : ∀ t, B.successProb t < 1)
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal)
    (seq : OptimalAllocationSequence (fun _ => B.toConsumptionModel)) :
    ∀ t : ItemType T,
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds
          (theorem3LogShareWeight B t /
            ∑ i : ItemType T, theorem3LogShareWeight B i)) := by
  have hlike_pos : ∀ t, 0 < B.likelihood t := by
    intro t
    rw [hpreference t]
    exact hpreference_pos t
  exact theorem3_varying_success_probability_log_share_formula
    B hprob_pos hprob_lt_one hlike_pos seq

terminal_result.expanded_type: Filter.Tendsto (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t) Filter.atTop (nhds (theorem3LogShareWeight B t / ∑ i : (Fin T), theorem3LogShareWeight B i))

Treat any listed local opaque/constant/axiom type head as requiring a checked carrier/refinement bridge before it is ordinary model data. Treat every opaque, ambiguous, tactic-body, or bounded terminal term path as requiring a checked semantic bridge before it is treated as an ordinary numeric or propositional result. Do not infer a source model from any local Lean name. For every dimension, record a source locator, a concrete semantic comparison, and Lean evidence; a detected support, joint-law/state-evolution, conditioning/calibration, expectation-definedness, null-cell/partition, or extended-rate shape also needs a checked bridge declaration or constructor route. For every detected probability-law surface, explicitly compare the source and Lean parameterizations rather than merely saying their parameters are positively related: state both scale/rate/variance conventions, the translation formula, and a checked law or outcome bridge. When the generated joint-law dimension requests source-carrier coherence analysis, identify the source and Lean random-variable carriers, explain why stagewise clocks are one joint source draw (or a source-defined kernel composition) rather than resampling, classify the measure transport, and record any all-rate family bridge. This individual row has an explicit source-presentation-selected direct map route. The association binds its byte-verified source item and current elaborated signature; it does not assert a direct/Spec structural equivalence.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded binder/result type surface
dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

expanded_shape_basis: generic, finite, subtype, or opaque carrier surface
expanded finite carrier requiring boundary-case review
dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded probability-law type with finite or ordered carrier
dimensions.required_check: For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded probability-law type surface
unexpanded or bounded terminal definition path requiring a semantic bridge
dimensions.required_check: Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate.

expanded_shape_basis: unexpanded or bounded terminal definition path requiring a semantic bridge
dimensions.required_check: State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

expanded_shape_basis: unexpanded or bounded terminal definition path requiring a semantic bridge
dimensions.required_check: For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

expanded_shape_basis: unexpanded or bounded terminal definition path requiring a semantic bridge
dimensions.required_check: For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

theorem proposition2_corrected_finite_and_sequence_source
    {T : ℕ} [NeZero T]
    (likelihood : ItemType T → ℝ) (kseq : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hlike_pos : ∀ t, 0 < likelihood t)
    (hkpos : ∀ N, 0 < N → 0 < kseq N)
    (hbound :
      ∀ N, 0 < N →
        (kseq N : ℝ) + 1 ≤
          (N : ℝ) * uniformSqrtMinShare likelihood - T)
    (seq :
      OptimalAllocationSequence
        (fun N => uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N))) :
    (∀ N, 0 < N → ∀ a : CountAllocation T,
      (uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N)).IsOptimalAtTotal N a →
        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood).Approx a
          ((2 * (Fintype.card (ItemType T) : ℝ) + 1) / (N : ℝ))) ∧
      seq.toAllocationSequence.ConvergesToProfile
        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood) := by
  constructor
  · intro N hNpos a hopt
    exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_finite_of_paper_bound
      likelihood N (kseq N) hNpos (hkpos N hNpos) hlike_pos a
      (hbound N hNpos) hopt
  · exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_sequence_homogeneity_of_paper_bound
      likelihood kseq hlike_pos hkpos hbound seq

binder_domains.expanded_type: ∀ N, 0 < N → (kseq N : ℝ) + 1 ≤ (N : ℝ) * uniformSqrtMinShare likelihood - T

terminal_result.expanded_type: (∀ N, 0 < N → ∀ a : (EconCSLib.Allocation ((Fin T))), (uniformTopKConsumptionModel likelihood (kseq N)).IsOptimalAtTotal N a → (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood).Approx a ((2 * (Fintype.card ((Fin T)) : ℝ) + 1) / (N : ℝ))) ∧ seq.toAllocationSequence.ConvergesToProfile (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood)

    (g : κ → ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (x : κ → ℝ) (a : κ → ℕ)

      (∀ i, 0 ≤ z i) → (∑ i : κ, z i) = (N : ℝ) →
        GeneralRounding.objective g z ≤ GeneralRounding.objective g x)

    (ha_opt : ∀ b : κ → ℕ, (∑ i : κ, b i) = N →
      GeneralRounding.objective g (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) ≤

        a t < ⌊x t⌋₊ + Fintype.card κ := by
  classical
  exact GeneralRounding.floor_count_close_of_strictConcave_maximizers
    g N x a hconc hx_nonneg hx_sum hx_opt ha_sum ha_opt

An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. checked_proof_steps.scope: The checked theorem visibly assumes Monotone h, B<0, sigma>0, eventual positive A-h, and positive weight for every type. It is a corrected-source result; it does not validate the printed B>0, sigma<0 statement or a zero-weight all-m conclusion.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: The phrase 'D has pdf f_D' is represented by a probability measure equal to Lebesgue volume with density ofReal(f_D), with f_D nonnegative, measurable, and integrable. These are not theorem-name consequences of a function called pdf: they require an actual density measure and enough boundedness/integrability for the expected top-k loss to be well defined. The source says only bounded above, so the nonnegative value-domain convention must remain visible rather than being inferred from the tail formula.

The source uses inconsistent iid wording, so the actual finite PMF and its expectation identities must be checked before asymptotic objective theorems receive source-model credit.

model_conventions.checked_scope: AllConsumedIidSource.lean derives the common-mean linear objective from a finite iid sample law. model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the all-consumed common-distribution endpoint, the common conditional mean is nonnegative for the weak argmax direction and positive for the unique argmax direction.
model_conventions.why_needed: When every item is consumed, the objective is linear in the common mean. A negative common mean reverses the stated argmax direction, and a zero mean eliminates uniqueness.

    (preferenceLaw : SourcePreferenceLaw T)
    (itemLaw : PMF Omega) (value : Omega → ℝ) {xTop xSecond : ℝ}

    (seq :
      OptimalAllocationSequence

          (TopKValueOracle.common T
            (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
              (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k))

    (hxTop_pos : 0 < xTop)

    (hsecond_le_top : xSecond ≤ xTop)
    (hsecond_lt_top : xSecond < xTop)
    (hvalue_nonneg : ∀ omega, 0 ≤ value omega)
    (hvalue_le : ∀ omega, value omega ≤ xTop)
    (hvalue_split : ∀ omega, value omega = xTop ∨ value omega ≤ xSecond)
    (htop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => value omega = xTop))
    (hnontop_mass_pos :
      0 < EconCSLib.pmfProb itemLaw (fun omega => ¬ value omega = xTop))
    (hpreference_pos : ∀ t : ItemType T, 0 < (preferenceLaw t).toReal) :
    (∀ a : CountAllocation T,
      ((TopKValueOracle.common T
        (finiteDiscreteIidTopKExpected Omega itemLaw k value)).toConsumptionModel
          (fun t => (preferenceLaw t).toReal) k).objective a =
        EconCSLib.pmfExp preferenceLaw
          (fun t =>
            EconCSLib.pmfExp
              (EconCSLib.pmfProduct (Fin (a.count t)) Omega itemLaw)
              (fun sample : Fin (a.count t) → Omega =>
                EconCSLib.Probability.sampleTopKSum
                  (fun i => value (sample i)) k))) ∧
      ∀ t : ItemType T,
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun N => CountAllocation.representation (seq.allocation N) t)
          Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (T : ℝ))) := by
  exact theorem1_i_finiteDiscrete_iid_exact_source_formula
    preferenceLaw itemLaw value k seq hk_pos hxTop_pos hxSecond_nonneg
    hsecond_le_top hsecond_lt_top hvalue_nonneg hvalue_le hvalue_split
    htop_mass_pos hnontop_mass_pos hpreference_pos

There are m types of items indexed by [m] = {1, 2, · · · , m}. A user prefers exactly one type of item, preferring
(t)
type t ∈ [m] with probability pt . The value of the i-th item of type t is a random variable Xi if the user
(t)
(t)
prefers type t and 0 otherwise (so its expected value is pt E[Xi ]). The recommender knows only how Xi
are distributed, not their realizations. We refer to pt as the likelihood of a type and the random variable
(t)
Xi as a conditional item value (the value of an item conditional on the user preferring the item’s type).
Let Sn,k be the set of n items that maximizes the expected total value of the k items with the highest
realized values. We call Sn,k the optimal set of n recommendations with respect to this objective. (We omit
the dependency of Sn,k on the other model parameters, as these will be clear from context.)
Sn,k arises naturally from an assumption that the user can only use k items, so that they derive value

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
Consider the setting in which Xi ∼ D, i.e., conditional item values are drawn from a shared distribution.
This implies that the values of items behave similarly across types and within types, and the platform cannot
easily distinguish between the items in a type. From the perspective of a hiring platform, there may be many
candidates with similar backgrounds (e.g., education or work history), none of whom can be distinguished
from another by the platform. Conditional on a recruiter preferring this background, candidate values can
be modeled as coming from a shared distribution.
We show that for a fixed k, as n grows large, the diversity of Sn,k theoretically varies between equal
representation, proportional representation, and near-complete homogeneity depending on the tail-behavior
of D. In particular, distributions that are bounded or have exponential tails induce at least proportional
representation. Meanwhile, Sn,n is completely homogeneous.

        (kseq N : ℝ) + 1 ≤

    (∀ N, 0 < N → ∀ a : CountAllocation T,

        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood).Approx a
          ((2 * (Fintype.card (ItemType T) : ℝ) + 1) / (N : ℝ))) ∧
      seq.toAllocationSequence.ConvergesToProfile
        (proposition2SqrtProfile likelihood) := by
  constructor
  · intro N hNpos a hopt
    exact proposition2_uniform_top_k_corrected_finite_of_paper_bound
